title: Minimal downtime incremental shared-state migration (notes)
summary: Working notes for an incremental upgrade strategy to migrate shared state (KV/ledger/cache) with minimal downtime for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus on compatibility shims, TF module adjustments, safe rollout windows and rollback triggers.
content:
Context:
This doc captures an approach for migrating the shared-state layer used by on-prem/private deployments (rocksdb/etcd backed ledgers, local KV caches, and prefix/KV caching in the serving runtime) while performing a runtime and control-plane bump. Goal: minimize customer-visible downtime and avoid state corruption.

High-level strategy (incremental + reversible):
1) Dual-read compatibility shim: deploy a shim that reads from new and old state backends and compares results (read-only) for a configurable percentage of requests.
2) Write-fanout phase (optional): for trusted clusters, fanout writes to both old and new backends but keep primary write destination unchanged until we validate parity.
3) Cutover window (short, coordinated): switch primary reads to new backend for canary subset, then progressively increase.
4) Rollback safe-path: ensure old backend can be promoted back to primary quickly; keep write multiplexing metadata to track last-writer.

Pre-upgrade checklist (ops + infra):
- Announce maintenance windows to customers (CS) and publish SLO exceptions.
- Snapshot existing state: run a full snapshot and upload to gs://redwood-backups/private-preupgrade-YYYYMMDD (Jenkins job: jobs/private/backup-snapshot).
- Verify terraform state health: terraform plan against remote state, ensure no pending locks.
- Confirm KMS/HSM keys for new control-plane components are accessible.
- Reserve operator nodes for manual intervention and have console access for on-prem clusters.
- Prepare rollback tickets (JIRA: ENG-2345 rollback runbook).

Terraform module notes (what to change / watch):
- Module path: modules/private/runtime-state-v1.8 -> create a new module runtime-state-v1.9 with additive changes only.
- Avoid renaming resources. If unavoidable, use terraform state mv in a pre-step with a dry-run. Document state-mv commands in ops playbook.
- Add feature-flag variable: enable_dual_read (bool) default = false. This allows toggling shim without a TF redeploy.
- Introduce new aws_lb_target_group healthcheck configs (on cloud-backed private) — increase healthy threshold for canary TGs to avoid flapping.
- If changing storage class (PVCs) on k8s nodes, add a pre-copy job and ensure pod disruption budgets are set to 0 for control-plane during copy.

Runtime compatibility concerns and mitigations:
- KV API v1 -> v2: keep compatibility adapter in runtime (reads accept both) for 4 weeks of canary traffic.
- KV/ledger replication lag: monitor replication_lag_ms; if > 200ms for > 5m, pause canary expansion and investigate.
- KV cache invalidation: after cutover, force prefix cache TTL = 1m for first hour to reduce staleness risk, then relax to normal policy.
- Model-serving KV lookups: add metrics to attribute responses to read source (old_vs_new) for automated check.

Canary rollout plan (recommended timeline):
- Phase 0 (prechecks, 0-4h): snapshots, TF plan/review, deploy dual-read shim to 0% traffic. Run smoke tests.
- Phase 1 (canary small, 4-6h): enable dual-read comparison on 1% of traffic. Capture mismatches over 2h.
- Phase 2 (write fanout, optional, 6-10h): enable write-fanout in a sandbox cluster only. Run consistency checks for heavy write scenarios (batch inference jobs).
- Phase 3 (canary expand, 10-16h): toggle primary read to new backend for 5% -> 25% over several hours if mismatch rate < 0.01% and replication lag < threshold.
- Phase 4 (full cutover, 16-24h): after 24h stable canary, switch remaining traffic and disable old backend; keep read-only shim running for 72h then remove.

Testing matrix (pre-merge + post-deploy):
- Unit tests: KV adapter, parity comparator logic.
- Integration: end-to-end inference path using local ledger snapshots. Test both recovery and leader failover scenarios.
- Chaos tests: node kill during write-fanout and verify ledger convergence.
- Performance: token-per-second benchmarks against canary TG; ensure p50 latency delta < 10% and p99 < 20% vs baseline.

Monitoring and SLOs to watch (alerts / dashboards):
- parity_mismatch_rate (should be < 0.01% during canary).
- replication_lag_ms (alert if > 200ms sustained).
- serving_p50/p95/p99_latency (alert on > 20% regression).
- errors_by_source (increase indicates incompatibility).
- consumer_error_rate (downstream product errors).
- infra_disk_io_saturation during pre-copy jobs.

Rollback playbook (fast path):
1) Pause traffic to canary TGs (AWS) or scale replicaSet to zero for k8s canary namespace.
2) Flip primary read flag back to old backend by setting runtime-config feature flag. This should be a single API call.
3) If writes were fanned-out, annotate new backend as read-only and drain write queues to old backend (scripts/ops/drain-writes.sh).
4) Run consistency reconcile job against snapshot and restore if corruption suspected.
5) Open postmortem ticket and notify affected customers.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: divergence between backends during write-fanout. Mitigation: keep fanout off by default and only enable in isolated clusters, run parity histogram checks every 30m.
- Risk: terraform resource renames causing recreate. Mitigation: state-mv plan and dry-run, avoid resource renaming; if unavoidable, schedule low-traffic window.
- Risk: cache stampede on cutover. Mitigation: warm caches in canary clusters and use rolling TTL policy.

Operator run commands (examples):
- snapshot: ./tools/backup.sh --cluster $CLUSTER --target gs://redwood-backups/private-preupgrade-$(date +%F)
- apply TF in plan-only mode: terraform -chdir=infra/private init && terraform -chdir=infra/private plan -var-file=canary.tfvars
- enable dual-read: curl -X POST "$CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/flags" -d '{\"enable_dual_read\":true,\"percent\":1}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide retention period for comparator logs (parity diffs) — large disk usage if kept for >7d.
- Confirm if on-prem customers with strict disk IO constraints need a non-copy migration path.
- Add CI job to simulate large ledger replay for performance regression checks.

Owners and responsibilities:
- Anika Patel: overall migration owner and ops lead.
- Marco Ruiz: terraform module changes and TF state migration plan.
- Samantha Chen: runtime compatibility adapter and parity comparator.
- Jared Lowe: observability + dashboards and alerts.

Post-upgrade validation checklist (within 72h):
- parity_mismatch_rate == 0 for production queries and any remaining mismatches resolved.
- running snapshot verified and stored.
- export of metrics to long-term storage and compare token-costs pre/post upgrade.
- collect customer feedback (CS) for any edge-case regressions.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the dual-read comparator conservative; store minimal payload (hashes) not full responses.
- If customers run air-gapped clusters, prefer staged runway with .tar snapshot transfers instead of live fanout.
- Coordinate with product if API surface changes require customers to re-pin SDK versions.

References and links: PR #4123 (runtime adapter), JIRA ENG-2345 (migration epic), internal confluence page (runtime-migration), and TF diff bucket in GCS listed above.

If we agree on this flow, next steps: draft TF changes, scope unit + integration tests, schedule dry-run in staging-onprem next sprint.
